Hudson Beat
HANUKKAH
COLOR BY NOTE
Rhythm values · Treble clef · Bass clef — 3 levels with answer keys
Grades 2–6 · 27 worksheets · 27 answer keys

Teacher Notes

Hanukkah Color by Note · 3 levels · grades 2–6

How to use

  • Pick a level for each student or group, print the worksheets single-sided, and hand out crayons or colored pencils.
  • Students read the symbol in each space, find it in the color key, and color the space. Every space has a symbol in it.
  • White in a key means leave the space white. Gray can be a gray crayon or a light pencil shade.
  • Check with the answer key that follows each level. Keys are full-color pages you can print or project.
  • All three levels use the same nine Hanukkah pictures, so one class can color the same picture at three different reading levels.

Great for

  • Early finishers and music centers
  • Sub plans (no music background needed with the answer keys)
  • A quick check of note-reading before or after Hanukkah and winter holiday lessons

Level guide

LevelSkillSuggestedPages
Level ARhythm valuesGrades 2–34–12 worksheets, 13–21 keys
Level BTreble clef notesGrades 3–522–30 worksheets, 31–39 keys
Level CBass clef notesGrades 4–640–48 worksheets, 49–57 keys

Level A: whole, half, quarter and eighth notes and the quarter rest. Level B: treble-clef notes from middle C (C4) to A5. Level C: bass-clef notes from E2 to middle C (C4). Ledger-line notes are included in levels B and C. Each key uses letter names, and the same letter can appear in two octaves.

Standards

Practices reading standard notation: note and rest values, and note names on the treble and bass staff. Supports the National Core Arts Standards for Music, Performing (reading notation, MU:Pr4.2) in grades 2–6.

What’s inside

Page 3: student reference (note values and note names). Level A: pages 4–12 worksheets, 13–21 keys; Level B: pages 22–30 worksheets, 31–39 keys; Level C: pages 40–48 worksheets, 49–57 keys. Last page: terms of use and credits. Pictures: 1. Menorah, 2. Dreidel, 3. Star of David, 4. Oil Lamp and Olive Leaves, 5. Three Dreidels, 6. Menorah in the Window, 7. Star Garland, 8. Star Medallion, 9. Menorah Under the Moon.

No songs, lyrics or copyrighted characters are used. All pictures are original line art.

Student Reference

Keep this page nearby while you color.

Level A · Note and rest values (beats in 4/4 time)

whole note4 beats
half note2 beats
quarter note1 beat
eighth note½ beat
quarter rest1 beat of silence

Level B · Treble clef note names

Lines (bottom to top): E G B D F · Spaces: F A C E · The first note, C, is middle C on a ledger line.

Level C · Bass clef note names

Lines (bottom to top): G B D F A · Spaces: A C E G · The last note, C, is middle C on a ledger line.

Stems

Notes below the middle line have stems going up on the right. Notes on or above the middle line have stems going down on the left. The stem never changes the note name: only where the notehead sits does.
